stem: Where is the ideal position for the tip of an umbilical venous catheter (UVC)?

options.text: At the level of the right hemidiaphragm or atrio-caval junction.
Deep within the right atrium of the heart.
To the left of the spine at the level of $T8$.
Within the portal vein in the liver.

explanation: The ideal position for a UVC is at the junction of the inferior vena cava and the right atrium.
rationale: Think about the point where the major vein from the lower body enters the heart.

optionExplanations.A: The ideal position for a UVC is at the junction of the inferior vena cava and the right atrium.
optionExplanations.B: The lecture notes that a tip extending into the atrium is too high, although it was shown as a common finding.
optionExplanations.C: The umbilical arterial catheter, not the venous catheter, typically resides to the left of the spine.
optionExplanations.D: Positioning in the portal vein is avoided to prevent complications; the catheter should pass through the ductus venosus to the IVC.

source.hint: Think about the point where the major vein from the lower body enters the heart.
